citations.passage:
IIIF gives archival viewers standardized deep-zoom image serving plus
manifests that carry page order and metadata; adopting it means a client's
scans stay portable across viewer implementations instead of locked to a
custom gallery.

Fifteen Dublin Core elements cover the descriptive fields the archive needs
— title, creator, date, subject, rights — without a bespoke schema; Quill &
Marrow drafted the house style on top of them for the Larkspur metadata.

judge.rationale: The answer correctly identifies iiif-overview as the note influencing d-011 and its relates_to connection to the archive-metadata notes and the fifteen Dublin Core elements with Quill & Marrow's house style. However, it omits the note's key rationale—that IIIF keeps a client's scans portable across viewer implementations—and adds an unsupported parenthetical list of specific Dublin Core elements.
